question: How do monthly income and expenses compare?

plan.title: Income and expenses by month
plan.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', date) AS month,
       round(sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE type = 'Income'), 2) AS income,
       round(sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE type = 'Expense'), 2) AS expenses
FROM company_finances
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY month
plan.explanation: Adds up the invoices sent (income) and the bills received (expenses) in each month.
assumptions: Amounts are before tax.
An invoice or bill counts in the month it was issued, not when it was paid.

question: What is our net profit by quarter?
aliases: how much profit did we make each quarter

plan.title: Net profit by quarter
plan.sql:
SELECT year(date) || ' Q' || quarter(date) AS quarter,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN type = 'Income' THEN amount ELSE -amount END), 2) AS net_profit
FROM company_finances
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY quarter
plan.explanation: Takes each quarter's income and subtracts everything spent in it: cost of sales, payroll, rent and other operating expenses.
assumptions: Amounts are before tax.
An invoice or bill counts in the month it was issued, not when it was paid.
No depreciation, interest or income tax: the data holds invoices and bills only.

question: What were our top expense categories in 2025?
aliases: where did we spend the most in 2025

plan.title: Spend by category, 2025
plan.sql:
SELECT category, round(sum(amount), 2) AS spend
FROM company_finances
WHERE type = 'Expense' AND year(date) = 2025
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY spend DESC
plan.explanation: Adds up 2025's bills by expense category, largest first.
assumptions: Amounts are before tax.

question: Which customers owe us the most?

plan.title: Unpaid invoices by customer
plan.sql:
SELECT counterparty AS customer,
       round(sum(amount + tax), 2) AS owed,
       count(*) AS invoices
FROM company_finances
WHERE type = 'Income' AND status <> 'Paid'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY owed DESC
LIMIT 10
plan.explanation: Adds up every invoice not yet paid, by customer, and shows the ten who owe the most.
assumptions: Owed includes tax: customers pay the invoice total.
Counts every unpaid invoice, whether or not it is past its due date.

question: How old are our unpaid invoices?

plan.title: Unpaid invoices by age
plan.sql:
WITH unpaid AS (
  SELECT amount + tax AS total,
         (SELECT max(date) FROM company_finances) - due_date AS days_late
  FROM company_finances
  WHERE type = 'Income' AND status <> 'Paid'
)
SELECT CASE WHEN days_late <= 0 THEN '0 days (not yet due)'
            WHEN days_late <= 30 THEN '1-30 days late'
            WHEN days_late <= 60 THEN '31-60 days late'
            WHEN days_late <= 90 THEN '61-90 days late'
            ELSE '90+ days late' END AS age,
       round(sum(total), 2) AS owed,
       count(*) AS invoices
FROM unpaid
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY min(days_late)
plan.explanation: Sorts the unpaid invoices by how far past their due date they are, and adds up what is owed in each group.
assumptions: “Today” is the last date in the data, 31 December 2025.
Owed includes tax: customers pay the invoice total.

question: What is our gross margin by quarter?

plan.title: Gross margin by quarter
plan.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('quarter', date) AS quarter,
       round((sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE type = 'Income')
              - sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE pl_group = 'Cost of sales'))
             / sum(amount) FILTER (WHERE type = 'Income'), 4) AS gross_margin
FROM company_finances
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY quarter
plan.explanation: Takes each quarter's income, subtracts the cost of sales (hosting, contractors and payment fees), and divides by the income.
assumptions: gross_margin is a fraction: 0.8 means 80% of income is left after the cost of sales.
Amounts are before tax.

question: How long do customers take to pay?

plan.title: Average days to get paid, slowest customers
plan.sql:
SELECT counterparty AS customer,
       round(avg(paid_date - date), 1) AS avg_days_to_pay,
       count(*) AS invoices
FROM company_finances
WHERE type = 'Income' AND paid_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY avg_days_to_pay DESC
LIMIT 10
plan.explanation: For each paid invoice, counts the days from the invoice date to the payment, then averages them by customer. The ten slowest are shown.
assumptions: Only paid invoices count: unpaid ones have no payment date yet.

question: How much does each department spend?

plan.title: Spend by department, 2025
plan.sql:
SELECT department, round(sum(amount), 2) AS spend
FROM company_finances
WHERE type = 'Expense' AND year(date) = 2025
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY spend DESC
plan.explanation: Adds up 2025's bills and payroll by department.
assumptions: Covers 2025, the latest full year in the data.
Amounts are before tax.

question: Where does our income come from?
aliases: what share of income comes from each category

plan.title: Income by category
plan.sql:
SELECT category, round(sum(amount), 2) AS income
FROM company_finances
WHERE type = 'Income'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY income DESC
plan.explanation: Adds up all invoices by what was sold: subscriptions, services, licenses and training.
assumptions: Covers every year in the data, 2023 to 2025.
Amounts are before tax.

question: What was our net cash flow each month?

plan.title: Net cash flow by month
plan.sql:
SELECT date_trunc('month', paid_date) AS month,
       round(sum(CASE WHEN type = 'Income' THEN amount + tax ELSE -(amount + tax) END), 2) AS net_cash_flow
FROM company_finances
WHERE paid_date IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY month
plan.explanation: Counts money in when a customer pays an invoice and money out when a bill is paid, then nets the two for each month.
assumptions: Cash moves on the payment date, including tax.
Unpaid invoices and bills are left out.

plan.explanation: Takes 2025's income and subtracts everything spent in 2025.
assumptions: Amounts are before tax.
No depreciation, interest or income tax: the data holds invoices and bills only.

question: Which vendors did we pay the most in 2025?
aliases: who did we pay the most

plan.title: Top vendors, 2025
plan.sql:
SELECT counterparty AS vendor, round(sum(amount), 2) AS spend
FROM company_finances
WHERE type = 'Expense' AND year(date) = 2025 AND category <> 'Payroll'
GROUP BY ALL
ORDER BY spend DESC
LIMIT 10
plan.explanation: Adds up 2025's bills by vendor and shows the ten largest. Payroll is left out: it isn't a vendor.
assumptions: Amounts are before tax.
